architecture.mechanism: Use of lightweight, recyclable metal sheets (aluminium/magnesium alloys) for automotive body panels to reduce vehicle mass and improve electrical grounding continuity through corrosion-resistant metallic interfaces.
architecture.intervention: Inspect the Mazda CX-5 engine compartment and battery tray for dissimilar-metal contact points (steel-to-aluminium or steel-to-magnesium joints typical of mixed-material construction) where galvanic corrosion or loose grounding straps could cause parasitic current draw; verify and re-torque all body-to-chassis ground bonds, particularly where lightweight alloy panels meet the steel battery negative return path.
architecture.expected_effect: Eliminating intermittent high-resistance or parasitic leakage paths across mixed-metal joints restores the battery's ability to hold charge during extended parking, resolving the sudden-discharge and post-shutdown buzzing symptoms.
architecture.falsification_test: Measure parasitic key-off draw with a clamp ammeter at the battery negative terminal before and after the grounding rework; also measure resistance between the engine block, body panels, and battery negative post. If parasitic draw remains above ~50 mA after repair, or if engine-to-chassis resistance exceeds ~0.1 ohm, the mixed-metal grounding mechanism is falsified.
